Troubleshooting

On this page 12 sections
  1. No Wi-Fi
  2. Hotel or airport Wi-Fi login page won't load
  3. The VPN blocks my home network
  4. An app can't see a folder or file
  5. Network protection blocked something
  6. Some apps failed to install during setup
  7. Sound problems
  8. An update broke something
  9. The computer boots to a black screen
  10. I forgot my login password
  11. Something is slow or the fan is loud
  12. How to get help

Most problems have a simple fix. Find your problem below. If nothing here helps, the last section explains how to ask for help.

Three quick helpers first. (1) Open Secure Linux Status & Fixes: a red or orange line often has a Fix it button. (2) Copy the error message (Ctrl+C) and open Explain This Error. (3) If the computer will not start at all, or a part seems broken, see "My computer is broken: how do I fix it?" and "Is every part of my computer OK?".

No Wi-Fi

  1. Check the Wi-Fi icon in the system tray (bottom-right). Make sure Wi-Fi is switched on and Airplane mode is off.
  2. Check whether the Wi-Fi radio is blocked: run rfkill list. If it says "Soft blocked: yes", run rfkill unblock wifi. "Hard blocked: yes" means a physical switch or a function key (often Fn plus a key with an antenna icon) has turned it off.
  3. Make sure NetworkManager has Wi-Fi on: nmcli radio wifi on.
  4. List nearby networks: nmcli device wifi list. Connect to one: nmcli device wifi connect "<network-name>" --ask. It asks for the Wi-Fi password.
  5. Restart the network service: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager.
  6. Still nothing? Plug your phone in with a USB cable and turn on USB tethering on the phone. The laptop will use the phone's internet. That gets you online to look up the fix.

Hotel or airport Wi-Fi login page won't load

Many public networks show a login page ("captive portal") before letting you online. They do this by hijacking DNS. Because this laptop uses encrypted DNS, the trick fails and the login page never appears. The VPN's kill switch can also block it. There is a one-click fix:

  1. Open Hotel / Cafe Wi-Fi Login from the app menu (or type secure-linux-hotspot in the terminal).
  2. It pauses the VPN and encrypted DNS and opens the login page. Log in.
  3. Press Enter in its window (or close it). Everything is put back exactly as it was. If you do nothing it returns by itself after 15 minutes.

If the login page still does not appear, open LibreWolf and go to a plain website such as http://neverssl.com. To pause only the encrypted DNS: secure-linux-dns open, and secure-linux-dns secure to switch it back on. See "Encrypted DNS and hotel Wi-Fi" in the tools chapter.

The VPN blocks my home network

With the kill switch on, NordVPN may block local devices: your phone (KDE Connect, LocalSend, Syncthing), your printer, or your home server (Immich, Pika Backup). Tell NordVPN to allow your home network's address range. For example, if your home addresses look like 192.168.1.x:

Terminal
nordvpn allowlist add subnet 192.168.1.0/24

If they look like 10.0.0.x or 10.x.x.x:

Terminal
nordvpn allowlist add subnet 10.0.0.0/8

Find your address with ip -4 addr (look at the inet line for your Wi-Fi). Newer NordVPN versions also have nordvpn set lan-discovery on, which allows all private local ranges at once. See your current settings with nordvpn settings.

An app can't see a folder or file

Flatpak apps are sandboxed. Some can only see certain folders. If an app can't open a file from another drive or folder:

  1. Open Flatseal.
  2. Pick the app on the left.
  3. Scroll to Filesystem. Turn on a broader option, or add the specific folder (for example /run/media for USB drives, or ~/Projects).
  4. Close and reopen the app.

Only give the access that is needed. "All user files" is reasonable for an editor. Avoid "All system files" unless you know why.

Network protection blocked something

If an app suddenly can't connect, you may have denied it in the "allow this app?" window, or a block list may have caught a website you need.

  1. Try secure-linux-netguard pause 15. If things work now, Network protection was the cause. (If not, look elsewhere.)
  2. Run secure-linux-netguard resume, then secure-linux-netguard why the-address.com to see whether a list has it. If you trust the address: secure-linux-netguard allow the-address.com.
  3. For an app you denied: open Network Monitor from the app menu. The Rules tab lists every rule. Find the rule for the app, double-click it, change the action to Allow, and save. Or delete the rule so it asks again.

The full story, including the honest note about the question window, is in "Network Monitor: which apps may go online".

Some apps failed to install during setup

Look at the Problems section of SETUP-REPORT.txt on your Desktop. The same list is kept in /var/log/secure-linux/failures.log. Most failures are caused by a brief internet problem or a busy server. Make sure you're online, then repair the setup: choose Repair setup in Secure Linux Status & Fixes, or run:

Terminal
sudo /usr/local/lib/secure-linux/setup.sh --repair

It is safe to run as often as you like. It skips what is already done and retries what failed. The full log is in /var/log/secure-linux/setup.log.

Sound problems

  • Click the speaker icon in the system tray. Check the right output is selected (speakers, headphones, HDMI, Bluetooth) and nothing is muted.
  • System Settings, Sound shows every device. It lets you pick the default output and input and test each speaker. It does the job of the classic "pavucontrol" volume control.
  • Easy Effects improves thin laptop speakers and noisy microphones with equaliser and noise-reduction presets. Open it, add effects, and leave it running.
  • Bluetooth headphones not working? Remove them in System Settings, Bluetooth and pair again.

An update broke something

Roll the system back to a snapshot from before the update. The easiest way is Repair This Computer, then Go back to an earlier snapshot (a snapshot of "now" is kept first). Or by hand:

  1. Open Btrfs Assistant.
  2. Go to Snapper, choose the root config, and pick a snapshot from before the problem.
  3. Click Restore and restart.

Your files in your home folder aren't affected. Alternatively, if one specific package caused it, find the update in dnf history list and run sudo dnf history undo <ID>.

The computer boots to a black screen

Usually a new kernel or graphics driver doesn't agree with your hardware. Fedora keeps the previous kernels installed.

  1. Restart. When the boot menu appears, use the arrow keys to choose the second entry, which is the previous kernel, and press Enter.
  2. If the menu doesn't appear, it is hidden because the last boot succeeded. Tap Esc or hold Shift just after the maker's logo disappears. After a failed boot, Fedora usually shows the menu automatically.
  3. Once you're in, update again (sudo dnf upgrade --refresh). A fixed kernel often arrives within days.

If it still won't start, use the repair tool: see "My computer is broken: how do I fix it?" (the USB stick's SystemRescue can repair the boot loader, rebuild boot files, or go back to an earlier snapshot).

Tip: make the boot menu always visible with sudo grub2-editenv - unset menu_auto_hide.

I forgot my login password

This is fixable, but you still need the disk-encryption password. Without that, nothing on the drive can be reached. Boot the USB stick, choose SystemRescue, and use Forgot my Linux login password in the repair menu (see "My computer is broken"); it walks you through it in plain steps. Prevention is easier: keep your login password in Bitwarden and on paper with your disk password.

Something is slow or the fan is loud

Open Mission Center and sort by CPU or memory to see what is busy. In the first hours after setup, Flatpak updates, ClamAV, Syncthing's first sync and Immich uploads can all be busy. That settles down.

How to get help

The Fedora community is friendly to beginners. Good places to ask:

  • ask.fedoraproject.org: the official Ask Fedora forum (part of discussion.fedoraproject.org).
  • r/Fedora on Reddit.
  • discuss.kde.org for desktop questions.

To get a good answer quickly, include:

  1. What you were doing, what you expected, and what happened instead.
  2. The output of fastfetch, which shows your Fedora version, hardware and desktop.
  3. A diagnostics file: open Create Diagnostics File from the app menu. It makes a zip on your Desktop with private details blanked out (still glance at it before sending).
  4. Recent errors: journalctl -b -p err (errors since this start). If the problem happened before the last restart, use journalctl -b -1 -p err.
  5. The exact error message, copied as text (Ctrl+Shift+C in the terminal), not retyped.

Before posting, check the output for anything private (your name, network names, email addresses) and blank it out. Never post passwords. Be wary of anyone who asks you to run long commands you don't understand, especially with sudo or curl ... | bash.

More

Prepare Windows and build the USB with Setup App

On this page 5 sections
  1. Choose only the work you want
  2. Back up to a separate drive
  3. Review the exact USB disk
  4. If Setup App is interrupted
  5. Next: boot and first login

BUILD-USB.cmd is the normal way to start. It opens the graphical Setup App with Windows administrator approval. You can review and untick steps before anything is downloaded or written. The app does not save passwords or write a stick while you are still reviewing.

Choose only the work you want

The steps start ticked where applicable: health, backup, Wi-Fi, browser passwords, app list, downloads, USB write, rescue tools, Debian and offline packs. Untick any you do not want. The health scan is read-only and reports Windows, CPU, RAM, disks and health, Secure Boot, battery, internet and disabled Wi-Fi. Enabling Wi-Fi is a separate reviewed opt-in.

  • SAVE-THIS-PC.cmd opens the same app in collect-only mode. USB write, rescue tools, Debian, downloads and offline packs are not offered as later writing stages.
  • SAVE-APPS.cmd runs only the read-only app scanner. Its record contains the computer hostname, collection time, and app names, publishers and sources — not documents, passwords or licence keys.
  • The login password needs at least eight English-keyboard characters. Wi-Fi can be typed, selected from saved Windows networks or skipped.

Back up to a separate drive

Choose a separate suitable drive with enough free space. The Windows system disk and Secure Linux stick are excluded. Ordinary backup skips private .ssh and .claude key folders and saved Wi-Fi passwords. Browser-password CSV export is a separate user action.

A requested backup must verify before later stages run. Verification checks every indexed file, its size and its full SHA-256, plus counts and manifest state. It is not a sample. Keep the backup drive disconnected after the check, and remember that an integrity check is not the same as a test restore.

Review the exact USB disk

  1. Read the proposed steps and the selected USB disk number, friendly name, exact byte size and stable ID.
  2. Tick the final review checkbox and choose Confirm. Only then does the app pass the reviewed disk identity and erase consent to the builder.
  3. The builder checks that identity again before writing. Do not rely on a drive letter alone.

The app shows a recommendation using its own RAM/architecture thresholds. Those are wrapper heuristics, not upstream speed or support promises. Debian is a separate boot-menu choice, not a Fedora profile.

If Setup App is interrupted

Reopen it and read the recovery review. The recovery schema stores only explicit non-secret state. Secrets and erase consent are cleared. Completed artifacts must match their path, size, SHA-256 and schema; a backup is fully verified again. The combined download/build stage always restarts with fresh secrets and erase review.

The browser CSV watch has a 600-second limit. Other parts have their own behaviour, so do not assume every operation waits forever. Progress weights and time estimates are display estimates only: they never choose, skip or time a step.

Next: boot and first login

The Ventoy menu has no countdown. Secure Boot enrolment, installation entries and troubleshooting are in Starting the USB stick on any computer. After installation, the first-run welcome has five screens and a final review; the longer migration topics stay available later.

Browsers & privacy

LibreWolf

fullliteBrowsers & privacy

A privacy-focused web browser based on Firefox, with the uBlock Origin ad blocker already built in.

LibreWolf is a version of Firefox with the tracking and data collection removed. It looks and works almost exactly like Firefox, so it will feel familiar if you have used Firefox or Chrome on Windows. It comes with uBlock Origin pre-installed, which blocks ads and trackers. It is installed as a Flatpak, so it runs in a sandbox.

Why it's here

It is your main everyday browser. It blocks ads and trackers out of the box, with no setup needed.

What to do next

LibreWolf

What it can do
  • Browse the web like Firefox or Chrome
  • Blocks ads and trackers with uBlock Origin
  • No telemetry sent to Mozilla
  • Stronger anti-fingerprinting than normal Firefox
  • Private windows
  • Supports Firefox add-ons such as the Bitwarden extension
  • Bookmarks, tabs and a reading view
  • Can import bookmarks from an HTML file
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher (bottom-left corner) and type LibreWolf.
  2. Click LibreWolf to open it.
  3. Click the uBlock Origin icon (a red shield) in the toolbar to see what it is blocking on a page.
  4. Open the menu (three lines, top right) and choose Settings to look through the privacy options.
  5. Install the Bitwarden extension from addons.mozilla.org so you can fill passwords.
  6. If you want to stay logged in to sites, change the cookie setting described in the gotchas below.
Everyday tips
  • Press Ctrl+T for a new tab and Ctrl+Shift+P for a private window.
  • If a site looks broken, click the uBlock Origin icon and turn it off for that site only.
  • Press Ctrl+D to bookmark a page.
  • Use Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen a tab you closed by mistake.
  • Downloads go to your Downloads folder by default.
  • LibreWolf updates through Discover, the software centre, along with your other Flatpak apps.
Privacy & security
  • uBlock Origin blocks most ads, trackers and many malicious sites.
  • By default LibreWolf deletes cookies and history when you close it, so sites forget you.
  • Network protection (OpenSnitch) already lets LibreWolf go online, so it should not ask. Ads, trackers and known malware sites are still blocked by its block lists.
  • Your DNS is already encrypted by the system, so you do not need to set up DNS-over-HTTPS in the browser.
  • Only install add-ons you trust. Each extra add-on is another thing that can see your browsing.
If something goes wrong
  • You get logged out of every site when you close the browser. Fix: in Settings, Privacy & Security, untick the option to delete cookies and site data when LibreWolf is closed, or add exceptions for the sites you use.
  • Some sites show the wrong time zone or look oddly sized. This is the anti-fingerprinting protection. It is normal and safe to ignore.
  • A site (often banking or video calls) will not work. Fix: turn off uBlock Origin for that site first. If it still fails, try it in a different browser.
  • You cannot save a download where you want. Fix: Flatpak apps can only see some folders. Save to Downloads, or use Flatseal to give LibreWolf access to another folder.
  • Firefox Sync is off by default. If you want it, look in Settings for the LibreWolf section and turn it on.

Learn more: https://librewolf.net/  ·  All apps

Tor Browser

fullliteBrowsers & privacy

A browser that hides who you are and where you are by sending your traffic through the Tor network.

Tor Browser is a modified Firefox that sends your traffic through three volunteer-run relays around the world before it reaches a website. The website cannot see your real IP address, and your internet provider cannot see which sites you visit. The app you install is a launcher: on first run it downloads Tor Browser itself and checks its digital signature so you know it is genuine.

Why it's here

For moments when you need strong anonymity, such as researching something sensitive. It is slower than a normal browser, so it is not meant for everyday use.

What to do next

Tor Browser

What it can do
  • Hides your IP address from websites
  • Hides the sites you visit from your internet provider
  • Visits .onion sites
  • Makes every user look alike to resist fingerprinting
  • Security level setting (Standard, Safer, Safest)
  • New Identity button to start fresh
  • Bridges to connect where Tor is blocked
  • Clears everything when closed
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Tor Browser.
  2. On the first run, wait while it downloads and verifies Tor Browser. This can take a few minutes.
  3. Network protection may ask about the download and later about the tor program. If a window appears, choose Allow.
  4. When the Connect to Tor screen appears, click Connect.
  5. Wait for the connection to finish. The first connection can take up to a minute.
  6. Browse as normal. Click the shield icon to change the security level if you want more protection.
Everyday tips
  • Expect pages to load more slowly than in LibreWolf. That is normal.
  • Keep the window at its default size. Resizing can make you easier to identify.
  • Use New Identity (in the menu) to close everything and start fresh.
  • Some sites show extra captchas or block Tor. Use LibreWolf for those.
  • Update when Tor Browser tells you an update is ready.
Privacy & security
  • Do not log in to your personal accounts in Tor Browser if you want to stay anonymous.
  • Do not install extra add-ons. They make you stand out.
  • Files you download (such as PDFs) can connect to the internet when opened outside Tor. Open them offline if you care about anonymity.
  • Tor hides where you are, but the last relay can see unencrypted traffic. Only use https sites.
If something goes wrong
  • The first run fails or says the signature could not be verified. Fix: check you are online, then close and open Tor Browser again to retry.
  • Tor will not connect. Fix: on the connection screen, use the connection assistant or choose a bridge, which helps on networks that block Tor.
  • It is very slow. This is the cost of anonymity. Try New Tor Circuit for this Site in the menu if one site is especially slow.
  • Network protection blocked something and Tor seems stuck. Fix: open Network Monitor, find the rule for tor or the launcher, and change it to allow.

Learn more: https://www.torproject.org/  ·  All apps

NordVPN

fullliteBrowsers & privacy

An optional paid VPN service designed to protect traffic between this computer and the VPN server.

NordVPN creates an encrypted tunnel from your laptop to a NordVPN server. Websites normally see the VPN server's address instead of yours, and the tunnel is designed to protect traffic contents from the local network and internet provider. You can control it with the NordVPN window or with the nordvpn command in the terminal. These are upstream capabilities, not an independent leak-protection guarantee from this guide.

Why it's here

It is available if you already choose and pay for this VPN service, including for reviewed use on public Wi-Fi.

What to do next

NordVPN (app launcher), or the nordvpn command in Konsole

What it can do
  • Connect to a VPN server with one command or click
  • Pick a country or city
  • Upstream kill-switch option intended to limit traffic if the VPN drops
  • Auto-connect when the laptop starts
  • Threat Protection Lite (blocks some ads and malicious sites)
  • Meshnet: link your own devices privately, if still offered on your plan
  • Show connection status
  • Graphical app and terminal commands
Getting started
  1. Open Konsole (the terminal) from the app launcher.
  2. Type nordvpn login and press Enter. A browser page opens. Sign in to your Nord account there.
  3. Type nordvpn connect to connect to a recommended server. Use nordvpn connect United_Kingdom (for example) to pick a country.
  4. Type nordvpn status to check the reported connection state.
  5. Type nordvpn set autoconnect on to ask it to connect when you start the laptop.
  6. Type nordvpn set killswitch on to enable NordVPN's upstream traffic-limiting feature. Check the reported state; this guide has not independently verified leak protection.
  7. If you prefer clicking, open NordVPN from the app launcher and use the window instead.
Everyday tips
  • nordvpn disconnect turns the VPN off.
  • nordvpn countries lists the countries you can pick.
  • nordvpn settings shows which options are on.
  • If a website blocks VPNs (some banks and streaming sites), try a different server or disconnect for that task.
  • Use NordVPN or Cloudflare WARP, not both at once; competing VPN routes can conflict.
Privacy & security
  • A VPN can protect traffic contents from the local network and internet provider, but NordVPN itself can see connection information. Choose a provider you trust and read its current privacy terms.
  • The kill switch is intended to reduce exposure if the connection drops; it is not an independently verified promise that no traffic or address can leak.
  • While connected, NordVPN may use its own DNS servers instead of the system's Cloudflare DNS. Check the active configuration rather than assuming which resolver is used.
  • A VPN does not stop you being tracked by cookies or logins. LibreWolf helps with that.
If something goes wrong
  • The nordvpn command says permission denied. Fix: your user must be in the nordvpn group. Run sudo usermod -aG nordvpn $USER, then log out and back in.
  • No internet at all after disconnecting. The kill switch may be blocking traffic. Check nordvpn status and settings, then reconnect or deliberately adjust the kill switch after reviewing the risk.
  • A hotel or cafe Wi-Fi login page will not appear. Open Hotel / Cafe Wi-Fi Login or run secure-linux-hotspot. It pauses the configured VPN/DNS protections for the sign-in window and restores the prior state afterwards.
  • KDE Connect, Syncthing or LocalSend stop finding your phone. Fix: the VPN can hide your local network. Run nordvpn set lan-discovery on, or disconnect while syncing.
  • Network protection asks about nordvpnd. It is pre-approved, so this is unlikely; if it asks, choose Allow, or the VPN cannot connect.

Learn more: https://support.nordvpn.com/  ·  All apps

Cloudflare WARP

fullBrowsers & privacy

A free, fast encrypted tunnel from Cloudflare that can also join a Cloudflare Zero Trust team.

WARP is Cloudflare's VPN-like app. It encrypts your traffic between the laptop and Cloudflare's network. Unlike NordVPN it is not mainly for hiding your location; it is for speed, safety on public Wi-Fi, and joining a Cloudflare Zero Trust team (for example, to reach a home server). It is controlled with the warp-cli command in the terminal.

Why it's here

It is an alternative to NordVPN and is needed if you use Cloudflare Zero Trust to reach your own private network. Use one or the other, not both.

What to do next

warp-cli (in Konsole)

What it can do
  • Encrypts traffic to Cloudflare's network
  • Free to use for personal use
  • Can join a Cloudflare Zero Trust team
  • Reach private networks set up in Zero Trust
  • Connect and disconnect from the terminal
  • Show connection status
Getting started
  1. First make sure NordVPN is off: run nordvpn disconnect.
  2. Open Konsole from the app launcher.
  3. For personal use, run warp-cli registration new. For a Zero Trust team, run warp-cli registration new your-team-name and finish signing in in the browser.
  4. Run warp-cli connect.
  5. Run warp-cli status to check it says Connected.
  6. When you are done, run warp-cli disconnect.
Everyday tips
  • warp-cli status is the quickest way to see if WARP is on.
  • warp-cli --help lists all the commands.
  • Switch back to NordVPN by running warp-cli disconnect first, then nordvpn connect.
  • If something odd happens, disconnect and connect again before trying anything else.
Privacy & security
  • WARP does not hide your country from websites the way a normal VPN does.
  • Cloudflare can see where your traffic goes while WARP is on. Read their privacy policy if this matters to you.
  • In a Zero Trust team, the team admin (you, if it is your account) can set policies that apply to this device.
  • Network protection already approves warp-svc. If it ever asks, choose Allow, or WARP cannot connect.
If something goes wrong
  • Internet breaks or is very slow. Fix: NordVPN and WARP are probably both on. Turn one off.
  • warp-cli says the registration is missing. Fix: run warp-cli registration new again.
  • Wi-Fi login pages at hotels do not appear. Fix: run warp-cli disconnect, log in to the Wi-Fi, then reconnect.
  • A command in an old online guide does not work. Cloudflare has renamed some warp-cli commands over time. Run warp-cli --help to see the current ones.

Learn more: https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/  ·  All apps

cloudflared

fullBrowsers & privacy

Cloudflare's tunnel tool, used here to reach your home server safely without opening ports on your router.

cloudflared is a terminal program from Cloudflare. On a home server it can create a Cloudflare Tunnel, which links the server to Cloudflare without opening your router to the internet. On this laptop it is mostly used as a client: it lets you sign in through Cloudflare Access and then reach that server, for example over SSH. There is no window; you use it in the terminal.

Why it's here

It lets you reach your home server from anywhere while keeping your home router closed to the internet.

What to do next

cloudflared (in Konsole)

What it can do
  • Connect to services behind Cloudflare Access
  • SSH to a home server through Cloudflare
  • Create and run Cloudflare Tunnels
  • Sign in to Cloudflare from the terminal
  • No router port forwarding needed
  • Works with Cloudflare Zero Trust policies
Getting started
  1. Set up the tunnel and an Access application for your server in the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard first.
  2. Open Konsole from the app launcher.
  3. Run cloudflared --version to check it is installed.
  4. To SSH through Access, run cloudflared access ssh --hostname ssh.yourdomain.com as the SSH proxy. Cloudflare's docs show the exact lines to add to your SSH config file.
  5. The first time you connect, a browser opens so you can sign in through Cloudflare Access.
  6. After signing in, the SSH connection continues as normal.
Everyday tips
  • cloudflared --help lists the main commands.
  • cloudflared access login https://your-app.yourdomain.com signs you in to an Access app ahead of time.
  • Sign-ins expire after a while. Just sign in again when the browser opens.
  • Keep cloudflared updated through normal system updates.
Privacy & security
  • Your home router stays closed. Cloudflare checks who you are before letting traffic through.
  • Protect your Cloudflare account with a strong password and two-factor codes from Ente Auth.
  • Anyone with your Cloudflare login could change your tunnel. Keep that account secure.
  • Network protection already approves cloudflared. If it ever asks, choose Allow.
If something goes wrong
  • SSH hangs or says the connection closed. Fix: check the tunnel is running on the home server and the hostname is spelled right.
  • The browser sign-in window never opens. Fix: copy the link cloudflared prints in the terminal and open it in LibreWolf.
  • Access says you are not allowed. Fix: check the Access policy in the Zero Trust dashboard includes your email address.
  • Guides online mix up server and client commands. On the laptop you normally only need the cloudflared access commands.

Learn more: https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared  ·  All apps

Ungoogled Chromium

fullBrowsers & privacy

A Chrome-like browser without Google services, kept for websites that only work in Chrome.

Ungoogled Chromium is the open-source base of Google Chrome with Google's services and tracking removed. LibreWolf is still your main browser; use this one for sites that need Chrome, such as Clipchamp or CapCut on the web, or sites that talk to USB devices (WebUSB or WebSerial). There is no Google account sign-in or sync.

Why it's here

Some web apps and device tools only work properly in Chrome-based browsers.

What to do next

Ungoogled Chromium (app launcher)

What it can do
  • Runs Chrome-only web apps like Clipchamp and CapCut web
  • WebUSB and WebSerial for device setup sites
  • No Google sync or Google account sign-in
  • Chrome-style developer tools
  • Can install Chrome extensions with extra steps
  • Private (incognito) windows
Getting started
  1. Open Ungoogled Chromium from the app launcher.
  2. Go to the website that needs Chrome, for example the Clipchamp or CapCut website.
  3. Sign in to that website if needed.
  4. If a site wants a USB device, plug it in and choose it from the browser's pop-up.
  5. Use LibreWolf for normal browsing, email and banking.
Everyday tips
  • Bookmark the few Chrome-only sites you need here.
  • There is no Chrome Web Store button. Installing extensions needs extra steps; see the project's FAQ.
  • Video editing in the browser uses your laptop's power; close other tabs for smoother playback.
  • Look in Settings to set the search engine you prefer.
Privacy & security
  • Google services are removed, but the websites you visit can still track you.
  • Clipchamp (Microsoft) and CapCut (ByteDance) are online services; treat anything you upload or sign into there as shared with them.
  • Only allow USB or serial access to sites you trust, and only for the device you expect.
  • Extensions are not auto-updated through a store, so update them yourself or keep very few.
If something goes wrong
  • USB device not found: Flatpak sandboxing may block it. Try allowing device access for this app in Flatseal, then restart the browser.
  • Netflix or other DRM video will not play: DRM support (Widevine) is not included. Use LibreWolf for those sites.
  • Cannot add extensions from the Chrome Web Store: this is expected; follow the project's extension instructions.
  • Cannot save or upload files from a folder: allow that folder in Flatseal.

Learn more: https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium  ·  All apps

Security

Bitwarden

fullliteSecurity

An open-source password manager that stores all your passwords in an encrypted vault and fills them in for you.

Bitwarden remembers your passwords so you only need to remember one master password. It works like the Bitwarden, LastPass or 1Password apps on Windows. There is a desktop app and a LibreWolf browser extension, and both use the same vault. Your vault is encrypted on your device before it is synced.

Why it's here

Strong, unique passwords for every site are the biggest single step for online safety, and Bitwarden makes that easy.

What to do next

Bitwarden

What it can do
  • Store passwords, cards, notes and identities
  • Fill logins in LibreWolf with the extension
  • Generate strong random passwords
  • Sync across laptop, phone and browser
  • Lock after a set time
  • Unlock with a PIN on this device
  • Import from other password managers
  • Show weak or reused passwords (some reports need a paid plan)
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Bitwarden.
  2. Log in with your Bitwarden email and master password, or create an account.
  3. In LibreWolf, go to addons.mozilla.org, search for Bitwarden, and add the extension.
  4. Log in to the extension too, then pin it to the toolbar.
  5. Visit a site, log in, and let Bitwarden offer to save the password.
  6. Set up two-step login for your Bitwarden account in the web vault settings.
Everyday tips
  • Use the password generator whenever you create a new account.
  • In LibreWolf, click the Bitwarden icon to fill a login on the current site.
  • Set a PIN to unlock quickly, and keep the master password for the first unlock.
  • Check the vault timeout in Settings so it locks when you step away.
  • Export a backup of your vault now and then and keep it somewhere safe.
Privacy & security
  • Your master password cannot be recovered by Bitwarden. Write it down and keep it somewhere physically safe.
  • Turn on two-step login. Store the recovery code offline.
  • Do not store the 2FA codes for your Bitwarden account inside Bitwarden itself. Use Ente Auth for those.
  • Network protection already lets Bitwarden sync. If a window asks anyway, choose Allow.
If something goes wrong
  • Biometric or browser-to-desktop unlock does not work. This is a known limit of the sandboxed Flatpak. Use the PIN or master password instead.
  • The extension and desktop app show different items. Fix: click Sync in each app (look in Settings or the menu).
  • Autofill does not appear on a site. Fix: open the extension and click the login, or check the saved website address matches.
  • Bitwarden will not sync. Fix: check that Network Monitor has not blocked it (Rules tab), and check the VPN is connected properly.

Learn more: https://bitwarden.com/help/  ·  All apps

Ente Auth

fullSecurity

An open-source app that shows your two-factor (2FA) login codes, with optional encrypted backup.

Many accounts ask for a 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds when you log in. Ente Auth makes those codes, like Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on a phone. It is open source and can back up your codes with end-to-end encryption, so you do not lose them if you lose a device. You can also use it without an account, offline only.

Why it's here

2FA codes protect your accounts even if a password leaks. Ente Auth keeps them safe and backed up, and works on both the laptop and your phone.

What to do next

Ente Auth

What it can do
  • Generate time-based 2FA codes
  • End-to-end encrypted backup and sync
  • Works offline without an account
  • Same codes on phone and laptop
  • Import from other authenticator apps
  • Encrypted export of your codes
  • Search and tag your codes
  • Lock the app
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Ente Auth.
  2. Choose to create an account (for backup) or use it offline.
  3. If you made an account, save the recovery key it shows you. Store it somewhere safe.
  4. On a website's security settings, turn on two-factor or authenticator app.
  5. In Ente Auth, add a new code and enter the secret key the site shows (the text under the QR code).
  6. Type the code from Ente Auth into the website to finish setup.
  7. Also save the website's own backup codes somewhere safe.
Everyday tips
  • Click a code to copy it, then paste it into the login page.
  • Install Ente Auth on your phone too, so you have the codes when the laptop is off.
  • Use the encrypted export now and then as an extra backup.
  • Give each entry a clear name so you can find it quickly.
Privacy & security
  • Your codes are encrypted before they leave your device. Ente cannot read them.
  • If you lose your password and recovery key, Ente cannot get your codes back.
  • Keep 2FA for Bitwarden here, not in Bitwarden itself, so one leak does not unlock everything.
  • If Network protection asks when Ente Auth first syncs, choose Allow if you use backup.
If something goes wrong
  • A code is rejected. Fix: your clock may be wrong. Codes depend on the correct time. Check the time in the system tray matches your phone.
  • You cannot scan a QR code on the laptop. Fix: ask the site to show the text secret key and type it in, or add it on your phone and let it sync.
  • Codes do not appear on the other device. Fix: make sure both are logged in to the same Ente account and online.

Learn more: https://ente.io/auth/  ·  All apps

Signal

fullSecurity

The desktop version of the Signal private messenger, linked to the Signal app on your phone.

Signal is an end-to-end encrypted messaging app, a private alternative to WhatsApp. The desktop app lets you send messages and make calls from the laptop. It needs Signal on your phone as the main device and links to it by scanning a QR code. This Flatpak is packaged by the community, not by Signal itself.

Why it's here

It lets you chat privately from the laptop with a full keyboard, using the same account as your phone.

What to do next

Signal

What it can do
  • End-to-end encrypted messages
  • Voice and video calls
  • Group chats
  • Send photos and files
  • Disappearing messages
  • Linked to your phone account
  • Notifications on the desktop
Getting started
  1. Make sure Signal is installed and set up on your phone first.
  2. Open the app launcher and type Signal.
  3. A QR code appears on the laptop.
  4. On your phone, open Signal, go to Settings, then Linked devices, then link a new device.
  5. Scan the QR code on the laptop screen with your phone.
  6. Give the laptop a name and wait for it to finish syncing.
Everyday tips
  • Old messages from your phone may not all appear on the laptop. Newer versions may offer to transfer recent history when you link.
  • Turn on disappearing messages for chats you want to keep tidy.
  • Signal Desktop must be opened at least every few weeks, or it may unlink itself.
  • Allow camera and microphone in Flatseal if calls do not work.
Privacy & security
  • Messages are end-to-end encrypted. Signal cannot read them.
  • Anyone who can use your unlocked laptop can read your Signal chats. Lock the screen with Super+L.
  • Check Linked devices on your phone now and then and remove any you do not recognise.
  • If Network protection asks when Signal first connects, choose Allow.
If something goes wrong
  • Signal says the device was unlinked. Fix: this happens after a long time offline. Link it again with the QR code.
  • Signal will not start after an update and mentions a database key or keyring. Fix: check the notes on the Signal page on Flathub, as this community build sometimes needs an extra setting.
  • Camera or microphone missing in calls. Fix: open Flatseal, pick Signal, and make sure device access is on.
  • Notifications do not show. Fix: check KDE System Settings, Notifications, and make sure Signal is allowed.

Learn more: https://signal.org/  ·  All apps

Tuta

fullSecurity

An encrypted email and calendar app, using your Tuta account (free plan).

Tuta (formerly Tutanota) is a private email service, like Gmail or Outlook but with end-to-end encryption. Your mailbox and calendar are stored encrypted, so Tuta cannot read them. The desktop app works like the Outlook app on Windows, but only for Tuta accounts.

Why it's here

It gives you a private email address and calendar that are not scanned for advertising.

What to do next

Tuta Mail (search Tuta in the app launcher)

What it can do
  • Encrypted email
  • Encrypted calendar
  • Contacts
  • Send password-protected emails to people outside Tuta
  • Search your mail
  • Desktop notifications
  • Free plan available
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Tuta.
  2. Log in with your Tuta address and password, or sign up for a free account.
  3. If you sign up, write down the recovery code it shows and keep it safe.
  4. Turn on two-factor authentication in Settings and add the code to Ente Auth.
  5. Click the calendar icon to see your calendar.
  6. Look in Settings to adjust notifications.
Everyday tips
  • Emails between Tuta users are encrypted automatically.
  • To send an encrypted email to a Gmail user, use the option to send it confidentially with a password, and share the password another way.
  • Keep the app open (or minimised) to get new-mail notifications.
  • The free plan has limited storage. Delete large attachments you no longer need.
Privacy & security
  • Your password and recovery code are the only way into your account. Tuta cannot reset your data without them.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication.
  • Normal emails to non-Tuta addresses are not end-to-end encrypted unless you send them with a password.
  • If Network protection asks when Tuta first connects, choose Allow.
If something goes wrong
  • You cannot add your Tuta account to Thunderbird or other mail apps. Tuta does not support IMAP. Use the Tuta app or website.
  • Free accounts that are not used for a long time can be deleted. Log in regularly, and check Tuta's current rules.
  • Notifications do not appear. Fix: make sure the app is running and check KDE System Settings, Notifications.
  • Cannot save an attachment where you want. Fix: save it to Downloads, or give Tuta more folder access in Flatseal.

Learn more: https://tuta.com/  ·  All apps

Network Monitor (OpenSnitch)

fullSecurity

Network protection: asks once about each new app that wants the internet, and blocks known malware, phishing and tracking sites.

Network Monitor is the window of OpenSnitch, an application firewall. Windows Firewall mostly guards the door for traffic coming in; this guards the door for traffic going out. On the main laptop it is on from the start. The first time a brand-new app wants to go online, a small window asks once (Always allow is pre-selected). Apps that came with the computer are already approved. Weekly-updated block lists stop known malware, phishing, tracker and telemetry sites for every app. It has two parts: a background service (opensnitch) and the window and pop-ups (opensnitch-ui).

Why it's here

It shows you exactly which programs talk to the internet, stops known-bad places for every app, and lets you block anything you did not expect. If it ever breaks it fails safe: your internet keeps working.

What to do next

Network Monitor (app launcher), or the shield icon in the system tray. Chapter: "Network Monitor: which apps may go online".

What it can do
  • A small "allow this app?" window, once per brand-new app
  • Pre-approved list for the apps and system services that came with the computer
  • Weekly-updated block lists for malware, phishing, trackers and telemetry
  • A message with Allow once, Always allow or Keep blocked when a list stops something
  • A weekly summary: "Blocked N connections this week"
  • Rules per program, address or port, which you can edit or delete
  • Live list of connections and statistics
  • Pause for 15 minutes to find out whether it is the cause of a problem
Getting started
  1. Network protection is on by itself. Look for its shield icon in the system tray (bottom right).
  2. When the "allow this app?" window appears, read the program name and the address. Click Allow for apps you know ("Always allow" is already selected).
  3. For anything you do not recognise, choose Deny. Nothing is lost; you can change your mind later.
  4. If a corner message says a site was blocked, choose Allow once, Always allow or Keep blocked. For malware and phishing sites it adds a warning.
  5. Open Network Monitor from the app launcher to see connections and rules. The Rules tab lets you change or delete a decision you regret.
  6. To check the state from the terminal: secure-linux-netguard status.
Everyday tips
  • You will rarely see questions: browsers, the VPN, updates, Syncthing, phone link and the photo app are already approved.
  • If something stops working, run secure-linux-netguard pause 15 and try again. If it works, run secure-linux-netguard why ADDRESS to see which list has it, then secure-linux-netguard allow ADDRESS if you trust it.
  • Honest note: the current Secure Linux steps do not establish what an ignored question window does, so do not rely on a timeout to make a safe choice. Answer the window deliberately. To make clicked answers last only until the next restart, run: sudo secure-linux-choice set netguard_prompt_duration restart. The background service and graphical question window are separate pieces of OpenSnitch; check current upstream behaviour before relying on a timeout result.
  • Right-click the Network Monitor menu entry for "Pause network protection for 15 minutes" and "Switch network protection back on".
  • Switch it off entirely with: sudo secure-linux-choice set opensnitch no (then Repair setup). Pros of leaving it on: visibility and block lists. Cons: the odd question and the occasional list false alarm.
Privacy & security
  • It only controls outgoing connections. firewalld handles incoming ones.
  • Malware can pretend to be a trusted program name. Check the full program path in the window.
  • Do not allow everything just to stop the questions. That removes the protection.
  • The block lists are downloaded on this computer from two public projects; nothing about you is sent. A broken or missing list blocks nothing.
  • On older (lite) PCs with 3 GB of memory or more only the quiet block lists run; it never asks. Below that it is left out. The atomic and Debian versions do not have it.
If something goes wrong
  • An app suddenly has no internet. Fix: you probably denied it. Open Network Monitor, go to Rules, find the app, and change or delete the rule. Or run secure-linux-netguard pause 15 to check.
  • A website you need is blocked. Fix: secure-linux-netguard why SITE, then secure-linux-netguard allow SITE (add --once 15 for just 15 minutes).
  • No questions appear at all. This is normal for pre-approved apps. If you expected one, open Network Monitor from the app launcher and check secure-linux-netguard status.
  • After an app updates, it may ask again if its program path changed. Allow it again if you trust it.
  • Flatpak apps may show paths starting with /app or a bwrap helper. That is normal for sandboxed apps.

Learn more: the matching chapter in this guide  ·  All apps

ClamAV + ClamTk

fullSecurity

An open-source virus scanner, with automatic signature updates, a weekly scan of Downloads, and a simple window for manual scans.

ClamAV is a virus scanner, a bit like Windows Defender but without real-time protection. It is mainly useful for checking files you download or receive, including Windows files you might pass on to others. ClamTk is a simple window for ClamAV so you can scan files and folders without the terminal. Virus signatures update automatically through the clamav-freshclam service.

Why it's here

Linux malware is rare, but downloaded files and email attachments can still carry threats, especially ones aimed at Windows users you share files with.

What to do next

ClamTk (app launcher), or clamscan in Konsole

What it can do
  • Scan a file or folder on demand
  • Automatic signature updates (clamav-freshclam)
  • Weekly low-priority scan of your Downloads and Desktop folders
  • Weekly scan results written to a log file
  • Never deletes files on its own
  • ClamTk window for scanning without the terminal
  • Terminal scanning with clamscan
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type ClamTk.
  2. Use the option to scan a file or scan a directory, and pick what to check.
  3. Wait for the scan to finish and read the results.
  4. To scan from the terminal, open Konsole and run clamscan -r ~/Downloads.
  5. The weekly scan results are in /var/log/secure-linux/clamscan/ (one file per week; read the newest with sudo less). If it finds something, Secure Linux Status says so.
  6. Signatures update by themselves. You do not need to do anything.
Everyday tips
  • Scan anything you download from an unfamiliar site before opening it.
  • Check the weekly log now and then. Look for lines ending in FOUND.
  • Scanning a big folder takes a while and uses a lot of the processor. The weekly scan runs at low priority to avoid slowing you down.
  • Run systemctl status clamav-freshclam to check updates are working.
Privacy & security
  • Scanning happens on your laptop. Your files are not uploaded anywhere.
  • Signature updates download from ClamAV's servers. Network protection already approves freshclam; if it asks, choose Allow.
  • ClamAV will not stop a threat as it runs. Safe habits matter more: only install software from Discover or trusted sources.
  • If a file is flagged, do not open it. Delete it yourself or ask someone you trust.
If something goes wrong
  • clamscan complains the database is missing or old. Fix: wait for freshclam to finish, or run sudo systemctl restart clamav-freshclam.
  • A safe file is flagged (false positive). This happens. Check the file name against the source, or upload it to a second opinion service if it is not private.
  • The weekly log says permission denied. Fix: read the files in /var/log/secure-linux/clamscan/ with sudo.
  • ClamTk looks dated or some options do nothing. It is a simple tool. The terminal clamscan command always works.

Learn more: https://www.clamav.net/  ·  All apps

Flatseal

fullliteSecurity

A simple app for viewing and changing what each Flatpak app is allowed to access.

Flatpak apps run in a sandbox, a bit like phone apps, and only get the access they ask for. Flatseal shows those permissions as on and off switches, like the app permissions screen on Windows or a phone. You can let an app see a folder, use the camera, or block its network access.

Why it's here

Many common problems with Flatpak apps (cannot open a file, no camera) are fixed in Flatseal, and it also lets you tighten privacy.

What to do next

Flatseal

What it can do
  • List every installed Flatpak app
  • See each app's permissions
  • Give or remove access to folders
  • Turn network access on or off
  • Allow or block devices such as camera
  • Reset an app back to its defaults
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Flatseal.
  2. Pick an app from the list on the left.
  3. Read through the switches on the right. Each one is a permission.
  4. To let an app see a folder, scroll to Filesystem and add the folder path.
  5. Close the app you changed and open it again so the change takes effect.
  6. If something breaks, use the reset button for that app.
Everyday tips
  • Change one thing at a time so you know what fixed a problem.
  • Give access to a specific folder rather than your whole home folder.
  • Changes only apply after you restart the app.
  • Flatseal only works for Flatpak apps, not normal system programs.
Privacy & security
  • Turning permissions off is safer. Turning them on gives the app more reach.
  • Be careful with full home folder or whole system access. It weakens the sandbox.
  • Some apps still work without network access, if you want them fully offline.
If something goes wrong
  • A change did nothing. Fix: fully close the app and open it again.
  • An app stopped working after a change. Fix: press the reset button for that app in Flatseal.
  • A system app is missing from the list. Only Flatpak apps appear in Flatseal.

Learn more: https://github.com/tchx84/Flatseal  ·  All apps

Lynis

fullliteSecurity

A terminal tool that checks your system's security settings and gives you a score and suggestions.

Lynis runs hundreds of checks on how the system is set up and reports warnings and suggestions. Think of it as a security health check, a bit like the Security section in Windows Settings, but much more detailed. It only reads and reports; it does not change anything.

Why it's here

It gives you an easy way to see how hardened the laptop is and spot anything that has drifted after changes.

What to do next

sudo lynis audit system (in Konsole)

What it can do
  • Full security audit of the system
  • Hardening index score
  • Warnings for serious issues
  • Suggestions for improvements
  • Detailed log file
  • Does not change your system
Getting started
  1. Open Konsole from the app launcher.
  2. Type sudo lynis audit system and press Enter.
  3. Enter your password when asked.
  4. Wait a minute or two while it runs its checks.
  5. Scroll up to read the Warnings and Suggestions sections.
  6. Note the hardening index near the end. Higher is better.
Everyday tips
  • Run it every month or after big changes, and compare the score.
  • The full details are saved in /var/log/lynis.log.
  • Do not try to fix every suggestion. Many are for servers and do not apply to a laptop.
  • Search the test ID (for example a code in square brackets) on the Lynis website to learn more about a suggestion.
Privacy & security
  • Lynis runs locally. It does not send your results anywhere.
  • It needs sudo to read system settings, but it only reads.
  • Be careful following random online advice to fix suggestions. Some changes can break the system.
If something goes wrong
  • The score is not 100. That is normal. A laptop does not need every server hardening option.
  • It warns about something set up on purpose (for example an open port for KDE Connect). That is expected.
  • The output scrolls past too fast. Fix: run sudo lynis audit system | less to page through it, and press q to quit.

Learn more: https://cisofy.com/lynis/  ·  All apps

Firewall (firewalld)

fullliteSecurity

The built-in firewall, set to block all incoming connections except the few apps that need them.

firewalld is the system firewall, like Windows Defender Firewall. It decides which incoming connections from the network are allowed. Here it uses the public zone, which blocks everything coming in by default. Only KDE Connect, Syncthing and LocalSend are allowed in, so they can find your phone and other computers. On old PCs, SSH is also open, protected by fail2ban.

Why it's here

It stops other devices on the same Wi-Fi or network from reaching services on your laptop.

What to do next

System Settings, then Firewall; or firewall-cmd in Konsole

What it can do
  • Blocks incoming connections by default
  • Allows KDE Connect (ports 1714-1764)
  • Allows Syncthing (22000 and 21027)
  • Allows LocalSend (53317)
  • SSH allowed on old PCs, with fail2ban blocking repeated bad logins
  • Manage from KDE System Settings or with firewall-cmd
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and type Firewall, or open System Settings and look for Firewall.
  2. Check the firewall is shown as enabled.
  3. To see the details in the terminal, open Konsole and run sudo firewall-cmd --list-all.
  4. Check that the active zone is public: run sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones.
  5. Leave it as it is unless an app's guide tells you to open a port.
Everyday tips
  • To open a port permanently: sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=1234/tcp, then sudo firewall-cmd --reload.
  • To close it again: sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=1234/tcp, then reload.
  • Only open ports you understand and actually need.
  • Run sudo firewall-cmd --state to check it is running.
Privacy & security
  • This firewall controls incoming traffic. Network protection (OpenSnitch) controls outgoing traffic. Together they cover both directions.
  • Every open port is a possible way in. Keep the list short.
  • On public Wi-Fi, the open ports are only reachable by devices on that same network. Using the VPN adds more protection.
  • On old PCs with SSH open, fail2ban temporarily bans addresses after repeated failed logins.
If something goes wrong
  • Changes vanish after a reboot. Fix: you forgot --permanent. Add it and run sudo firewall-cmd --reload.
  • A new app cannot be reached from your phone or another PC. Fix: the firewall is blocking it. Check the app's docs for its port and open only that port.
  • KDE Connect, Syncthing or LocalSend cannot find devices. Fix: check the ports are still listed with sudo firewall-cmd --list-all, and check the VPN is not hiding your local network.
  • The KDE Firewall page and the terminal disagree. The terminal (firewall-cmd) is the most reliable view.

Learn more: https://firewalld.org/  ·  All apps

Encrypted DNS and network privacy

fullliteSecurity

System-wide settings that encrypt your DNS lookups, block known malware sites, and make your laptop harder to track on Wi-Fi.

DNS turns website names into addresses. Normally these lookups are sent in plain text, so anyone on the network can see which sites you visit. Here, systemd-resolved sends them encrypted (DNS-over-TLS) to Cloudflare 1.1.1.2, which also blocks known malware sites, with Quad9 as a backup. The laptop also uses a different random Wi-Fi hardware (MAC) address for each network, does not announce its name, and uses IPv6 privacy addresses.

Why it's here

It protects your browsing from snooping on public Wi-Fi and blocks many dangerous sites for every app, not just the browser.

What to do next

Nothing to open. Check it in Konsole with resolvectl status

What it can do
  • Encrypted DNS (DNS-over-TLS) for all apps
  • Malware site blocking via Cloudflare 1.1.1.2
  • Automatic fallback to Quad9
  • Random Wi-Fi MAC address per network
  • Laptop name not announced on the network
  • IPv6 privacy addresses
  • Works without any app to open
Getting started
  1. This is already set up and runs by itself.
  2. To check it, open Konsole and run resolvectl status.
  3. Look for 1.1.1.2 in the DNS servers and +DNSOverTLS in the settings.
  4. Test a lookup with resolvectl query example.com.
  5. If a site is blocked as malware, it simply will not load. That is the protection working.
Everyday tips
  • You do not need to change DNS settings in browsers or apps.
  • When NordVPN is connected, it may use its own DNS instead. That is fine.
  • Each Wi-Fi network sees a different MAC address for your laptop, but the same one each time you return to it.
  • If a single site will not load but others do, it may be blocked as malware. Be cautious.
Privacy & security
  • Your internet provider and Wi-Fi owner cannot see your DNS lookups.
  • Cloudflare (or Quad9 as backup) can see your lookups. Both publish privacy policies and say they do not sell this data.
  • Encrypted DNS does not hide your IP address. Use NordVPN for that.
  • The random MAC address makes it harder to track the laptop across different Wi-Fi networks.
If something goes wrong
  • A hotel, cafe or airport Wi-Fi login page never appears (captive portal). Fix: open Konsole and run sudo rm /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/10-encrypted-dns.conf && sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved, then log in to the Wi-Fi. Afterwards, turn encrypted DNS back on with sudo /usr/local/sbin/setup.sh <profile> <user> (use full or lite and your username).
  • No websites load but you are connected. Fix: run sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved. If that fails, try the captive portal fix above.
  • A work or school network requires its own DNS. Fix: use the captive portal fix while on that network, and turn it back on afterwards.
  • A site you trust is blocked. Cloudflare's malware list can occasionally be wrong. Contact Cloudflare or use a different network temporarily.

Learn more: https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/  ·  All apps

Disk encryption (LUKS2)

fullliteSecurity

Full-disk encryption that keeps your files unreadable without your disk password, even if the laptop is stolen.

Your disk was encrypted with LUKS2 when Linux was installed. This is like BitLocker on Windows. Every time you power on, you type the disk password before the system starts. Without it, nobody can read your files, even by removing the drive.

Why it's here

If the laptop is lost or stolen, your files, passwords and accounts stay protected.

What to do next

Nothing to open. Manage it in Konsole with cryptsetup

What it can do
  • Encrypts the whole system disk
  • Password asked at every power-on
  • Protects data if the laptop is lost or stolen
  • Add a backup passphrase
  • Change the passphrase
  • Uses the modern LUKS2 format
Getting started
  1. Power on and type your disk password when asked. Then log in as normal.
  2. Find your encrypted partition: open Konsole and run lsblk -f. Look for the line with type crypto_LUKS, for example nvme0n1p3.
  3. Add a backup passphrase: run sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey /dev/nvme0n1p3 (use your own partition name).
  4. Enter an existing passphrase first, then the new backup one twice.
  5. Write the backup passphrase down and keep it somewhere safe, away from the laptop.
  6. To change a passphrase: run sudo cryptsetup luksChangeKey /dev/nvme0n1p3 and follow the prompts.
Everyday tips
  • Encryption only protects the laptop when it is fully powered off. Shut down, rather than sleep, when travelling.
  • Use a long passphrase made of several words. It is easier to remember and harder to guess.
  • Your disk password and login password can be different.
  • Keep regular backups of your important files. Encryption does not protect against a broken drive.
Privacy & security
  • There is no recovery if you forget every passphrase. Your data is lost for good.
  • Add a backup passphrase and store it somewhere physically safe.
  • When the laptop is on and unlocked, files are readable. Lock the screen with Super+L when you step away.
  • Never type your disk password into a website or a message.
If something goes wrong
  • The password is rejected at power-on. Fix: the keyboard layout at that screen may be US. Check symbols like @ and quote marks. Caps Lock may also be on.
  • You picked the wrong partition for cryptsetup. Fix: it will say it is not a valid LUKS device. Run lsblk -f again and use the crypto_LUKS one.
  • The password screen does not appear and the screen is black. Fix: try pressing Esc or an arrow key, the prompt may be hidden behind the boot logo.
  • Forgot the passphrase and have no backup. There is no fix. You would need to reinstall and restore from backups. This is why the backup passphrase matters.

Learn more: https://gitlab.com/cryptsetup/cryptsetup  ·  All apps

Art & creative

ArtCraft

fullArt & creative

A free, open-source family of creative 'Crafting Apps' installed through the ArtCraft Launcher, plus a web-based AI studio.

ArtCraft is an open-source (Apache-2.0) creative project. On this laptop the ArtCraft Launcher was installed, and it installs a set of 15 native Crafting Apps that run on Linux. The separate ArtCraft Studio, which uses generative AI, has no Linux version, so you use it in a web browser at getartcraft.com instead.

Why it's here

It adds a bundle of free creative tools in one place, and gives you a way to try AI image tools without installing anything heavy.

What to do next

ArtCraft Launcher (app launcher)

What it can do
  • One launcher that installs and opens the Crafting Apps
  • 15 native Linux Crafting Apps
  • Keeps the Crafting Apps up to date from the launcher
  • ArtCraft Studio (generative AI) in the web browser
  • Free and open source (Apache-2.0)
  • Works alongside GIMP, Krita and Inkscape for finishing work
Getting started
  1. Open the app launcher and start ArtCraft Launcher.
  2. Look through the list of Crafting Apps it shows.
  3. Open one Crafting App and try it with a small test project.
  4. Save your work into a folder you can find again, such as Pictures or Documents.
  5. For the AI studio, open LibreWolf and go to getartcraft.com.
  6. Only upload images you are happy to share, because the AI may run on someone else's server.
Everyday tips
  • Start the Crafting Apps from the launcher so you always get the installed version.
  • Check the launcher now and then for updates.
  • Finish or touch up results in GIMP, Krita or Inkscape.
  • Keep a dedicated folder for ArtCraft projects so they are easy to back up.
  • If you are unsure what a Crafting App does, look at its menus and the project website.
Privacy & security
  • It is not clear whether ArtCraft Studio's AI runs on your computer or in the cloud, so treat anything you upload there as not private.
  • Do not upload photos of people, documents or anything personal to the web studio.
  • Network protection may ask when the launcher first tries to reach the internet; allowing it is needed for downloads and updates.
  • The launcher came from the official GitHub project (storytold/craft-launcher); avoid installing copies from other websites.
If something goes wrong
  • Looking for ArtCraft Studio in the app menu? It has no Linux app; use it on the web at getartcraft.com.
  • A Crafting App will not download or update: check that Network Monitor did not block the launcher and that you are online.
  • AI features feel slow: web AI depends on their servers and your internet speed, not your laptop.
  • Can't find a saved file: look in the app's Save dialog to see which folder it uses by default.

Learn more: https://getartcraft.com  ·  All apps

GIMP

fullArt & creative

A powerful free photo editor and image manipulation program, the closest free match to Photoshop.

GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program) edits photos and images with layers, masks, selections and filters, much like Photoshop. It can open PSD files, though complex Photoshop features such as smart objects and some adjustment layers will not come across fully. The menus and shortcuts are different from Photoshop, so expect a short learning curve.

Why it's here

You used Photoshop, and GIMP covers most everyday photo editing, retouching and compositing for free.

What to do next

GIMP (app launcher)

What it can do
  • Layers, layer masks and blend modes
  • Selections: rectangle, ellipse, free, fuzzy and by colour
  • Crop, resize, rotate and perspective correction
  • Healing and clone tools for retouching
  • Curves, levels and colour adjustments
  • Text layers
  • Opens and exports PSD, PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF and more
  • Large library of filters and effects
  • Plug-ins and scripts for extra features
Getting started
  1. Open GIMP from the app launcher.
  2. Use File > Open to open a photo.
  3. Open Windows > Dockable Dialogs > Layers if the Layers panel is not visible.
  4. Try a simple edit, such as Image > Scale Image or the Crop tool.
  5. Use File > Save to keep an editable GIMP file (.xcf) with all layers.
  6. Use File > Export As to make a normal JPEG or PNG for sharing.
Everyday tips
  • Save = GIMP's own .xcf format. Export As = JPEG/PNG. This is the biggest difference from Photoshop.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes, and Edit > Undo History shows every step.
  • Press Tab to hide the panels and see more of your image.
  • Hold Ctrl and scroll to zoom; press 1 for 100% zoom.
  • If a panel goes missing, look under Windows > Dockable Dialogs.
  • Use layer masks instead of erasing, so you can undo changes later.
  • Search for 'GIMP Photoshop shortcuts' if you want familiar keys; shortcuts can be changed under Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts.
Privacy & security
  • GIMP works completely offline; your images never leave the laptop.
  • As a Flatpak it is sandboxed. If it cannot see a folder or drive, give it access in Flatseal.
  • Exported photos can keep camera data (EXIF), including GPS location. Check the metadata options in the export dialog before sharing online.
If something goes wrong
  • Pressed Ctrl+S and got an .xcf file instead of a JPEG: use File > Export As (Ctrl+Shift+E) instead.
  • Painting does nothing: make sure the right layer is selected and there is no active selection somewhere else (Select > None).
  • A PSD looks wrong: effects and smart objects from Photoshop are not fully supported; flatten them in Photoshop first if possible.
  • Cannot open files from a USB drive or other folder: grant access to that location in Flatseal.
  • Very large images feel slow: 16 GB RAM is fine for normal photos, but huge multi-layer files will be slower.

Learn more: https://www.gimp.org  ·  All apps

Krita

fullArt & creative

A professional free painting and drawing app made for digital artists.

Krita is built for drawing and painting rather than photo editing. Think of it like Photoshop's painting side, or apps such as Clip Studio Paint or Procreate. It has many realistic brushes, works well with pen tablets, and can even do simple frame-by-frame animation.

Why it's here

It is one of the best free tools for digital painting, illustration, comics and concept art.

What to do next

Krita (app launcher)

What it can do
  • Hundreds of brushes with pressure support for pen tablets
  • Layers, masks and blend modes
  • Brush stabiliser for smooth lines
  • Symmetry and drawing assistants for perspective
  • Frame-by-frame animation with onion skin
  • Comic panel and text tools
  • Opens and saves PSD files
  • Exports PNG, JPEG, and animation (GIF or video)
  • Customisable workspaces
Getting started
  1. Open Krita from the app launcher.
  2. Choose File > New and pick a canvas size (for example 3000 x 2000 pixels).
  3. Pick a brush from the Brush Presets panel on the right.
  4. Draw on the canvas. Use Ctrl+Z to undo.
  5. Add a new layer from the Layers panel before each new part of your drawing.
  6. Save with File > Save to keep a .kra file with layers.
  7. Use File > Export to make a PNG or JPEG to share.
Everyday tips
  • Right-click on the canvas to open the pop-up palette with your favourite brushes and colours.
  • Press E to switch the brush into eraser mode.
  • Hold Space and drag to move around the canvas.
  • Hold Shift and drag to resize the brush.
  • Use Window > Workspace to switch layouts, for example for animation.
  • Krita autosaves backups; check Settings > Configure Krita if you want to change how often.
Privacy & security
  • Krita works offline; your art stays on the laptop.
  • As a Flatpak it is sandboxed. Use Flatseal if it cannot reach a folder or external drive.
  • Only install brush packs and resources from sources you trust.
If something goes wrong
  • Pen pressure does not work: check your tablet in System Settings and try Settings > Configure Krita > Tablet settings.
  • Painting does nothing: you may be on a locked or hidden layer, or have a selection active (Select > Deselect).
  • Canvas is mirrored or rotated: check the View menu to reset rotation and mirror.
  • Very large canvases or long animations get slow: lower the size or close other apps; 16 GB RAM has limits.

Learn more: https://krita.org  ·  All apps

Inkscape

fullArt & creative

A free vector drawing app, the closest free match to Adobe Illustrator.

Inkscape makes vector graphics: shapes and lines that stay sharp at any size, just like Illustrator. Its main file format is SVG, which is also what most cutting machines (such as Cricut or Silhouette) and laser cutters accept. It is great for logos, stickers, signs, icons and cut files.

Why it's here

You used Illustrator, and Inkscape covers logos, layouts and SVG cut files for free.

What to do next

Inkscape (app launcher)

What it can do
  • Draw shapes, lines and curves with the Pen (Bezier) tool
  • Edit nodes and paths precisely
  • Combine shapes (union, difference, intersection)
  • Text, including converting text to paths
  • Trace a bitmap image into vector shapes
  • Layers and object alignment tools
  • Saves SVG; exports PNG and PDF
  • Makes clean SVG files for cutting machines
Getting started
  1. Open Inkscape from the app launcher.
  2. Set the page size in File > Document Properties.
  3. Draw a rectangle or circle with the tools on the left.
  4. Change fill and outline colour in Object > Fill and Stroke.
  5. Add text with the Text tool.
  6. Save with File > Save As and choose Inkscape SVG.
  7. Use File > Export to make a PNG for sharing.
Everyday tips
  • For cut files: select your text and use Path > Object to Path so the machine does not need your fonts.
  • Use Path > Union to merge overlapping shapes into one cut line.
  • Path > Trace Bitmap turns a simple picture into vector shapes.
  • Plain SVG (File > Save As > Plain SVG) is often the most compatible choice for other apps.
  • Use Object > Align and Distribute to line things up neatly.
  • Press 5 to fit the whole page on screen.
Privacy & security
  • Inkscape works offline.
  • As a Flatpak it is sandboxed. Use Flatseal if it cannot open files from a folder or USB stick.
  • Only open SVG files from sources you trust, like any document.
If something goes wrong
  • Cutting machine shows the wrong size: check the document units (mm or inches) in File > Document Properties before saving.
  • Text looks different on another computer: convert text to paths (Path > Object to Path) before sharing.
  • Your cutting machine's own software may not run on Linux. You can design in Inkscape, save the SVG, and upload it from a computer or web app the machine supports.
  • Illustrator .ai files open only partly: save them as PDF or SVG from Illustrator first if you can.

Learn more: https://inkscape.org  ·  All apps

Darktable

fullArt & creative

A free photo organiser and RAW photo editor, similar to Adobe Lightroom.

Darktable manages your photo library and lets you develop photos, especially RAW files from cameras. Like Lightroom, it is non-destructive: your original photo is never changed, and edits are stored separately. It has two main views: Lighttable for browsing and Darkroom for editing.

Why it's here

It gives you Lightroom-style photo editing and organising without a subscription.

What to do next

Darktable (app launcher)

What it can do
  • Import and organise photos with ratings, colour labels and tags
  • Edit RAW files from most cameras
  • Exposure, white balance, colour and tone adjustments
  • Cropping, rotation and lens correction
  • Local adjustments with masks
  • Copy edits from one photo to many

  • Export to JPEG, PNG, TIFF and more
Getting started
  1. Open Darktable from the app launcher.
  2. In Lighttable, use the import module (left side) to add a folder of photos.
  3. Double-click a photo to open it in Darkroom.
  4. Try the exposure module and the crop module first.
  5. Go back to Lighttable (press L) when finished.
  6. Select photos and use the export module on the right to save JPEGs.
Everyday tips
  • Press D for Darkroom and L for Lighttable.
  • Use the history panel on the left to step back to any earlier version.
  • Edits are stored in small .xmp files next to your photos; keep them together when moving files.
  • Rate photos with number keys 1 to 5 to sort the keepers.
  • Use the search box in the modules panel to find a module by name.
  • Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy and paste edits between photos.
Privacy & security
  • Darktable works offline; photos stay on your laptop.
  • As a Flatpak it is sandboxed. Use Flatseal if it cannot see a photo folder or SD card.
  • Exported photos can include GPS location. Check the metadata settings in the export module before sharing online.
If something goes wrong
  • Too many modules and options: start with exposure, crop, color calibration and filmic or sigmoid; ignore the rest at first.
  • Photo looks different from the camera preview: RAW files start plain; that is normal.
  • Cannot find the original photo: Darktable only links to files; it does not move them. Check where you imported from.
  • Slow previews: some modules are heavy on integrated graphics. Edits still work, just slower.
